subject: Dedicated cluster: throughput guardrails & preemption window — request for explicit SLA language
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@heliocare.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated cluster: throughput guardrails & preemption window

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the dedicated pool looks promising. Before we proceed to procurement, procurement and infra asked for clearer language around two items that are blocking our legal approval:

1) Preemption / maintenance behavior: we need to understand what happens when nodes are preempted for maintenance or hardware reclaim. Will our reserved GPUs ever be preempted during heavy sustained traffic, and if so how long is the "preemption window" where throughput may degrade while backend balancing occurs?

2) Baseline throughput guarantees: we ran standard load tests with your team last month and captured a baseline p95 throughput per reserved GPU. We need a contractual minimum throughput floor (e.g., a % of baseline) for dedicated pools, or a clear crediting mechanism if throughput drops below that floor for > N minutes.

I've attached our baseline-throughput-report.csv and would appreciate Redwood's suggested SLA sentence(s) we can pass to legal. Also curious if you can include an operational resilience paragraph describing fallbacks (model variant downgrade, routing to burst capacity, queued request behavior).

Oliver
Procurement Manager, Heliocare Systems

Attachment: baseline-throughput-report.csv (text/csv)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@heliocare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster: throughput guardrails & preemption window

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear note. Appreciate the CSV; that helps a lot.

Short answer up front: we can propose contract language that defines a throughput guardrail and an operational resilience clause. Two quick clarifications before I draft suggested wording:
- Is Heliocare aiming for a hard throughput floor (creditable) or a best-effort target with credits tied to sustained degradation?
- Do you expect non-preemptible hardware across the entire committed fleet, or is a limited preemption allowance during urgent maintenance acceptable (e.g., up to 15 minutes per event)?

Ben / Lauren — looping you in for commercial/legal context. I can draft a 2-paragraph SLA blurb and an operational playbook excerpt after Oliver confirms the above.

Thanks,
David
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@heliocare.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@heliocare.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster: throughput guardrails & preemption window

Hi David — thanks for the quick response.

Answers:
- We prefer a hard floor that is creditable. Our regulators want a predictable baseline for customer-facing latency/throughput. Credits can be capped, but there needs to be a measurable, enforceable metric.
- Non-preemptible across the committed pool is strongly preferred, but we can accept a defined maintenance preemption window if it's both limited in duration (<= 20 minutes per event) and scheduled with at least T+60 notice where possible.

Please include any fallback behavior Redwood supports (e.g., automatic routing to burst capacity in another region, temporary downgrade to quantized model variant, or a queued grace runway) in the operational paragraph.

Oliver

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated cluster: throughput guardrails & preemption window

All — quick internal draft language below for discussion. Marissa, can you validate the technical ops paragraph? Lauren, is the crediting formulation commercially acceptable?

Proposed SLA excerpt (commercial):
"Redwood shall maintain a sustained throughput equal to at least 92% of the Customer's agreed baseline p95 throughput per reserved GPU over any rolling 60-minute window. If sustained throughput for Customer's Dedicated Pool falls below 92% of baseline for a continuous period exceeding 30 minutes, Customer shall be eligible for service credits equal to 5% of the monthly Dedicated fee per 30-minute interval (capped at 50% of monthly fee per calendar month)."

Operational resilience paragraph (ops):
"In the event of scheduled maintenance or emergency hardware preemption affecting reserved GPUs, Redwood will: (a) provide at least 60 minutes' advance notice for scheduled maintenance when feasible; (b) initiate automatic routing to Customer's configured burst capacity or to verified cross-region standby pools; (c) transparently downgrade to an agreed quantized model variant with documented output parity tolerances if routing capacity is exhausted; (d) enable a short 'grace runway' queuing mode for in-flight requests up to 120 seconds to avoid request failures while routing/fallbacks complete."

Notes:
- We hedge the commercial floor at 92% to reflect realistic tail behavior while still offering crediting.
- The ops paragraph includes a 120s queued grace runway — Marissa, confirm feasibility for your SRE playbook.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated cluster: throughput guardrails & preemption window

Ben / team — technical sign-off and a couple of suggested tweaks:

1) Throughput floor: 92% p95 over rolling 60m is doable as a commercial metric, but we should be explicit that baseline measurements must be agreed and recorded monthly. Add: "Baseline p95 throughput shall be measured over the 30-day period preceding contract start and recalculated on a monthly cadence with Customer approval."

2) Preemption: Non-preemptible SKUs are available for dedicated pools in our 'Resilient' offering. If the customer takes standard dedicated SKUs, we must keep the 20-minute emergency preemption allowance. Recommend we offer an optional 'Resilient' add-on (non-preemptible) that matches Heliocare's regulator preference.

3) Grace runway / queueing: 120s queuing for in-flight requests is technically feasible, but we should cap queued requests per tenant to avoid head-of-line blocking. Suggest: "Queued grace runway will be subject to a tenant-level cap of 500 concurrent queued requests; excess requests will receive a 429 with an estimated retry-after."

I'll return a redlined SLA paragraph and an ops playbook excerpt (one page) — attaching a draft SLA PDF that incorporates the measurement language.

Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: dedicated-sla-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@heliocare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster: throughput guardrails & preemption window

Oliver — attaching our proposed SLA language and a one-page ops playbook excerpt for Heliocare's review. Highlights:
- Commercial: 92% p95 throughput floor over rolling 60m; crediting kicks in after 30 continuous minutes under the floor; cap at 50% monthly.
- Measurement: baseline measured in 30 days prior to contract start and recalculated monthly with your approval.
- Preemption: optional 'Resilient' non-preemptible SKU available; standard dedicated SKU allows limited emergency preemption (<= 20 minutes) with T+60 notice where feasible.
- Ops: automatic routing to burst/cross-region standby, quantized-model fallback, 120s queued grace runway with tenant cap of 500 concurrent queued requests.

If that aligns with Heliocare's requirements, Lauren can coordinate final wording with legal and Ben will follow up on pricing for the 'Resilient' add-on.

Thanks,
David

Attachments: dedicated-sla-draft-v1.pdf, baseline-throughput-report.csv (as previously sent)
